newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures slip minutes before close.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures slip minutes before close.

text.p: The Key December Euroyen futures contract slipped minutes before the close on Friday, after spending most of the day at its Thursday level.
Some dealers attributed the last-minute fall to rumours of a leak in Japan industrial output data for July, which was officially announced at 3.30 p.m (0630 GMT), the time the market closed.
But there was no evidence of a leak, they said.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said Japan's industrial production grew a preliminary 4.1 percent in July month-on-month. This was at the top end of market expectations, dealers said.
Apart from the brief spurt of activity before the close, the December was mostly steady at 99.30. The day's range was between 99.28 and 99.33.

A tumble in Tokyo share prices sent the December higher early in the morning, but it failed to hold on, hit by a series of offers. "The December was felt to be capped after we saw lots of offers at 99.31," said a city bank trader.
Meanwhile, the March contract did not meet market expectations, failing to take over the benchmark status as its volume failed to exceed the December's.
In the interbank market, a majority of overnight call money was traded at 0.47 percent, the level which traders said was likely to be the weighted average of the rate for the day.

A tug of war between the week-end factor, namely the rate's tendency to fall on Friday, and the month-end factor, which is stronger-than-usual fund demand, was central to the market today, dealers said.
The winner seemed to have been month-end fund demand, which led to a rise in the rate by one basis point from Thursday's 0.46 percent, they added.
The BOJ's morning operation was neutral as expected. It injected 400 billion yen into the market, traders also said.
In the open market, CD rates were steady from Thursday.
About 80 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) have been issued at 0.54 percent.
One-month CDs were also issued at 0.54 percent, in volume of 75 billion yen. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.53 percent.
